title: FORTY DAYS AND THE WRITING OF GOD

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Then the Lord said to Moses, 'Write down these words, for in accordance with these words I have made a covenant with you and with Israel.' Moses was there with the Lord forty days and forty nights without eating bread or drinking water. And he wrote on the tablets the words of the covenant - the Ten Commandments." - Exod 34:27-28 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
"Write down these words." God's covenant was not left to memory or oral tradition. It was written, fixed, preserved — so that generations who never stood at Sinai could know exactly what God had said.

That is why we have a Bible. God chose to speak, and He chose to have it written down. All Scripture is God-breathed and useful (2 Tim 3:16), and it was written for our instruction so that through endurance and encouragement we might have hope (Rom 15:4).

Forty days and nights without food or water is beyond natural survival. This was a sustained man in a sustained encounter with God. It also quietly echoes forward: Israel forty years in the wilderness, Elijah forty days to Horeb, and Jesus forty days in the desert without food, where He answered the tempter by quoting the very words Moses was given (Matt 4:4).

Moses spent forty days receiving God's words. Jesus spent forty days standing on them.

We may not have mountaintop experiences, but we hold in our hands what Moses carried down that mountain. The question is whether we treat it as God's own writing.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. How much time do you actually give to God's written Word?
2. Do you read Scripture as God speaking, or as background reading?
3. What one passage could you know deeply enough to stand on under pressure?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You that You have spoken and that Your words are written for me. Give me hunger for Your Word. Amen.
